cases.layer: API/SQLite with canonical inert-runtime currentness; native provider zero
cases.given: One registered binding, exact session A with a canonical blocking request addressed to the operator, exact distinct session B with canonical SUBMITTED plus committed current started proof. Choose a visual agent filter that retains A's work but hides B's work item.
assertions: Prove the filter really hides B in the visible Work selection; do not assume it from labels.
Compare complete private operation/progress keys before and after the visual filter; exact B remains present.

GET harness-board presentation_version=2 with that same filter: original full binding tuple unchanged, activity working, running_sessions value 1, blocks_harness false, blocking partial, request A still correctly scoped.
After canonical terminal B, a fresh filtered GET may move A to waiting_user/full block; no new turn is admitted by a read.
Read-only canonical-table snapshots remain equal around GETs; first setup/binding/grant and session IDs stay exact.
cases.readiness: Requires reviewed composition of the two existing canonical inert-runtime helpers. copy_session/add_parallel_running_read_fact do not copy a valid lease and must NOT manufacture live authority. If the complete fixture cannot be built with existing owners, qualify only the private-query filter invariant and leave A06 API/presentation partial explicitly.
cases.browser_remaining: Apply the actual visual filter in the browser and inspect unchanged binding, Working status and independently reachable request without selecting latest.

cases.layer: Historical synthetic migrated SQLite facts + actual ASGI HTTP; not native execution proof
cases.given: The existing exact fixture-success operation has the parameterized terminal receipt and a schema-valid historical execution_results capture anchored to its own session/epoch/sequence event. The captured text contains a short, unique partial-output marker.
assertions: GET /home/results returns the same source operation ID and exact server/executor/workspace/session/operation target, not a newly generated result or successor.
Outcome and delivery_semantics.execution_outcome are exactly failed/cancelled; task_state and verification remain not_applicable; no approval evidence is invented.
Preview equals the complete short partial-output marker, truncated false, content_state available, regardless of unsuccessful productive outcome.
GET exact target remains available and still points to that same operation; repeated GETs preserve all productive rows, receipts, capture and message delivery/ACK state.
cases.readiness: Straight extension of existing schema-valid capture fixture; insert the referenced historical event before execution_results. No canonical_frame, watermark, native prompt or real failure/cancel claim is fabricated.
cases.browser_remaining: Open the exact failed/cancelled delivery, read the partial output, and assert no generic productive replay CTA. Prior R5 browser outcome checks do not replace these literal partial-output assertions.

cases.layer: SQLite/HTTP Results and auxiliary preference transition
cases.given: At least three result identities in project A and a result in B; limit=1 guarantees selected result is off the first page. The selected result carries exactly three linked artifact references. It is older than 24 hours and initially unseen.
assertions: Traverse real cursors to locate selected ID; prove it is absent from page one and reachable, not inferred from an initial preview.
Before seen, old selected result is retained by unseen preference; its three exact artifact IDs appear once each, same claim/workspace, with no private paths.

Use the exact occurrence attention_id, source_revision and preference_revision through canonical /attention/{id}/seen; wire the fixture Home and Attention services to the same migrated store, not different DBs.

Only that preference changes. Other off-page and project-B occurrences retain their individual seen state; no message_deliveries row/ACK, claim, grant, receipt, decision, operation or capture changes.
Fresh retained feed applies the 24-hour rule to the now-seen selected result; old cursors conflict if the global revision changes, and reread starts from a new snapshot without merging revisions.
Exact legacy historical result/target remains reachable according to existing detail contract even if the retained board feed no longer includes it.
cases.readiness: Three linked metadata references can reuse the grouping fixture. This does not assert managed artifact content retrieval; actual artifact API/store proof is a separate existing layer. Verify preference events separately from productive tables rather than claiming the entire DB is immutable.
cases.browser_remaining: Open the off-page delivery and all three artifact affordances, mark seen and observe retained-feed refresh while keeping exact historical context; no inbox ACK request.

cases.layer: Actual ASGI denial responses over the migrated Results fixture
cases.given: Read an own result containing a unique synthetic protected-output marker, then alter only server, explicit workspace fence, session or operation in its exact target.
assertions: Wrong server or mismatched explicit workspace fence returns CONFLICT/409; nonexistent exact session or operation returns NOT_FOUND/404, according to current service branches.
Denied JSON has no data payload, protected marker, preview, artifact path or summary/count fields; no success-shaped empty inventory is returned.
Canonical productive-row snapshots remain identical across the forged GETs.
Do not invent per-workspace ACL for the global operator; the negative is exact scope/reference mismatch or a genuine unauthorized agent transport.
cases.browser_remaining: Forged direct URL/panel navigation must render denial with no protected preview/counter and no fallback to another item.

cases.layer: SQLite projection + actual application/json response; no browser execution claim
cases.given: An own public workspace/agent label has a bounded synthetic hostile HTML/ANSI marker; a separate private Bearer-style token appears only in the designated private input/metadata.
assertions: Actual HTTP response is application/json and parses normally; public label remains a bounded string according to the existing projection contract.
Private marker, request auth payload and provider/filesystem paths do not occur in serialized public Home/selector data.
No productive operation or process is started by these GETs; compare canonical tables and the inert fixture's native-open count.
Do not demand HTML encoding in the JSON API or assume a raw public string executed. HTML/ANSI rendering safety is tested separately in a real browser.
cases.browser_remaining: Use real DOM textContent and script/global marker checks plus console/network observations; ensure no HTML handler/ANSI execution or protected token disclosure. HTTP JSON/header checks alone do not qualify this.

cases.layer: Canonical native-request fixture + Home exact read + actual decision rejection
cases.given: Obtain one actual canonical input request, its original Home exact target and decision CAS/revision. Revoke its own grant or make the admitted authorization revision stale using the established negative-fixture contract; do not create or widen authority.
assertions: Repeat the original stale decision body, not a new intent: current HTTP authority denies 403/409 and creates no new operation/decision/outbox row.
Re-read the same exact Home target: historical context, when authorized, must preserve its old IDs; do not require history to disappear merely because live action authority expired.
Fresh operational state/allowed actions no longer claim current execution/response authority from the revoked scope.
Full canonical table snapshot after the explicit revocation remains unchanged by stale POST and passive GETs; old request, result and references remain auditable.
cases.readiness: This closes the revoked-authority combination, not the literal successor-with-same-name browser case. The latter needs a genuinely created second session and explicit old-target action/selection checks; never invent it by renaming an ID.
cases.browser_remaining: Keep the old panel open through genuine revocation/successor creation; reject stale action and never select the successor by name/latest.
